p: The ad presents a workflow demonstrating Artifact Share, where a user reviews an AI-generated design doc, adds a comment requesting a shorter timeline, runs a CLI command to apply comments, and views the updated document at the same URL with the thread marked resolved.
Artifact Share lets teams review AI-generated specs via interactive comments on a single URL, allowing coding agents to update the doc directly.

The ad effectively communicates the workflow loop between human reviews and agent edits on a single URL. Text scaling remains mostly readable, though dense UI moments push mobile limits. Audio support and pacing are modest but clear.

Review at one URL. Any agent.'), diluting the any-agent/same-URL message","CLI frame (frame-2) drops the Artifact Share wordmark, breaking persistent branding for one full beat"]

The comment → CLI edit → republish sequence clearly demonstrates the core mechanic (humans point, agents edit, same URL), and the UI mockups are clean and legible with no artifacts. But nothing in frame 0 works as a hook — it's just a decision doc with no headline copy, so the 'who reviews it' tension from the creative brief never lands visually. The closing card also swaps in generic SaaS messaging instead of the specified CTA, weakening message-to-brief alignment even though it's still coherent and on-brand.
